result:
Riley, I graded your first attempt (`s1`): **2 correct, 2 partly correct and 2 wrong.** Feedback for each answer is in `grades/0001-s1.json`.

| Item | Verdict | Main point |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | An agent is a model working in a loop. |
| q2 | Wrong | The model asks for a tool to be used, and your program runs it. |
| q3 | Correct | A step limit stops a loop that's going nowhere. |
| q4 | Wrong | There are 4 model calls: one for each of the three tool requests and one for the final answer. |
| q5 | Partly correct | You said the result goes back to the model, but not why. It's so the model can choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | Partly correct | You're right that the model uses tool names and descriptions. It doesn't remember earlier sessions on its own, though. |

**The main thing to fix is who does what.** The model only writes text, either a tool request or an answer. Your program runs the tool, sends back the result and calls the model again. This matters for your design, because your code is what accesses the booking system, and each extra model call adds cost.

There's also a separate point from q6. If the assistant needs information from an earlier session, your program has to save it and give it to the model again. That leads into context and memory, the next topic for your project.

**Next step:** take the request "Is the laser cutter free Friday, and am I trained to use it?" Write out each step, label it "model" or "program", then count the model calls, assuming the model asks for one tool per call. If you send me your steps here, I can check them.

I also added a [learning record](learning-records/0003-model-runs-tools-misconception.md) about the tool-running mix-up and updated `NOTES.md`. These reflect only your first attempt. I haven't graded your later one (`s2`), so it may show you've since improved. You can ask me to grade it next.
